{{short description|Swiss mathematician}}
'''Ernst Alfred Ruh''' (born 23 February 1936) is a Swiss mathematician, specializing in differential geometry.

Ernst Ruh received his doctorate in 1964 from [[Brown University]] under [[Katsumi Nomizu]] with thesis ''On the Automorphism Groups of a G-structure''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=4373}}</ref> He is a professor at [[Ohio State University]] and a professor of computer science at the [[University of Basel]] (1987/89).<ref name="Mathch">Bruno Colbois, [[Christine Riedtmann]], Viktor Schroeder: ''Math.ch/100'', European Mathematical Society 2010, {{ISBN|3037190892}}, p. 347</ref> In 1990 Ruh became a full professor (professor ordinarius) of mathematics at the [[University of Fribourg]]; he was the successor of Josef Schmid.<ref name="Mathch" /> He retired in 2006 as professor emeritus.

His name is attached to the [[Gromov-Ruh theorem]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Ruh, Ernst A.|year=1982|title=Almost flat manifolds|journal=Journal of Differential Geometry|volume=17|issue=1|pages=1–14|mr=658470|doi=10.4310/jdg/1214436698|doi-access=free}}</ref> He was an [[invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] at Berkeley in 1986. He became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2012.
